skill.name: write-feature-docs
skill.description: Creates first-pass Warp feature documentation from product and technical specifications, verifies claims, confirms scope interactively, captures approved screenshots, and opens a draft docs pull request.
skill.summary: Turn a Warp feature specification into a reviewed MDX documentation draft and draft pull request.
skill.author: warpdotdev

security_audit.summary: Most detections are Markdown backticks, code fences, relative links, or benign GitHub examples and are false positives. The fixed pull request body path creates a local tampering risk, and optional UI capture can expose sensitive data when images enter a public documentation change. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The pull request body uses the predictable shared path /tmp/pr-body.md.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary file with mktemp, restrict permissions, pass that path to gh, and remove it immediately after use.

remediation.issue: Accepted screenshots can contain sensitive information before they are added to public documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Use a sanitized test account and require explicit human approval of each final image before adding, committing, or pushing it.

content.value_statement: Feature specifications do not automatically become accurate, publishable documentation. This skill verifies implementation details, confirms audience and structure, drafts MDX, and prepares a reviewable pull request.
actual_capabilities: Locates PRODUCT.md and TECH.md specifications and separates public behavior from internal implementation details.
Verifies feature flags, UI labels, settings paths, commands, shortcuts, and related pages through repository research.
Builds a content design plan and waits for engineer confirmation before outlining.
Creates a complete MDX draft using the selected Warp documentation template and style rules.
Attempts optional screenshots with privacy, framing, legibility, and retry checks.
Prepares a branch, documentation changes, and a draft pull request with reviewer context.
limitations: Requires an interactive engineer for separate content plan and outline confirmations.
Targets Warp repositories, templates, review gates, and documentation conventions.
Cannot verify product intent, unreleased behavior, or confidential details without engineer input.
Requires repository access, GitHub CLI authentication, and optional computer use for screenshots.

use_cases.title: Document a shipped feature
use_cases.description: Convert an approved product or technical specification into an accurate first-pass documentation page.

use_cases.title: Reduce documentation research
use_cases.description: Verify implementation details and isolate only the questions that require subject matter expertise.

use_cases.title: Prepare a reviewable update
use_cases.description: Create or update an MDX page and open a structured draft pull request for editorial review.

prompt_templates.prompt: Document [feature] using [spec ID]. Prefer updating [existing page], verify UI paths, then present the content plan and outline separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add a feature to documentation that already covers the related surface.

best_practices: Keep the engineer present for separate content plan and outline confirmations.
Validate feature and specification tokens before using them in shell or GitHub searches.
Mark unresolved claims clearly and exclude confidential implementation details from public drafts.
anti_patterns: Do not run the workflow unattended or combine the two required confirmation stages.
Do not publish technical specification details before an engineer confirms they are public.
Do not include screenshots containing private repositories, credentials, personal information, or customer data.

faq.question: Does this skill work without a product specification?
faq.answer: Yes. It researches the relevant repository first, then asks targeted questions about gaps that code cannot resolve.

faq.question: Can this skill run automatically after every release?
faq.answer: No. It requires an interactive engineer. Warp uses the separate missing_docs workflow for release-triggered documentation.

faq.question: Which documentation formats does it produce?
faq.answer: It produces MDX pages based on Warp templates for feature, conceptual, procedural, reference, troubleshooting, quickstart, or guide content.

faq.question: How does it protect confidential technical information?
faq.answer: It flags internal implementation details from TECH.md and requires engineer confirmation before including them in public documentation.

faq.question: Are screenshots required?
faq.answer: No. Screenshot capture is optional. Failed, unavailable, unsafe, or unverified captures remain explicit placeholders for a documentation reviewer.

faq.question: What access does the workflow require?
faq.answer: It needs relevant repository access and GitHub CLI authentication. Screenshot capture also needs an available computer use tool.
